paper.title: Science mock test: forces, pressure, digestion and breathing
paper.sub: Ember · 30 minutes · 33 marks · pen, pencil, ruler, calculator
paper.intro: Calculations: write the equation, then the numbers, then the answer with its unit. Explanations: one mark per link, so join your ideas with so.

blocks.q: 1. A box has a weight of 400 N. Its base has an area of 0.8 m². Calculate the pressure the box puts on the floor. Give the unit.
2. Explain why it hurts more to be stood on by someone in high-heeled shoes than in flat trainers, even though their weight is the same.
3. A sealed balloon is put in a hot room. It gets bigger. Use ideas about particles to explain why.
4. State what happens to atmospheric pressure as you climb a mountain, and give one reason why.
5. Name the organs that food passes through, in order, from the mouth to the anus.
6. Explain how the small intestine is adapted to absorb food quickly.
7. Fibre is not digested. Explain why it is important to eat a fibre-rich diet.
8. A spring is 5 cm long. A force of 3 N stretches it to 8 cm. (a) What is the extension? (b) The spring obeys Hooke’s Law. What would the extension be with a 6 N force?
9. A parachutist opens her parachute. Explain why she slows down and then falls at a steady speed.
10. Give one way to reduce friction and one way to reduce drag.
11. Explain how air is moved into and out of the lungs. Use the words volume and pressure in your answer.

selfcheck: Every calculation shows the equation and a unit.
Every explanation has its links joined with “so”.
Q11 covers breathing in and out, with volume and pressure.
I wrote down which questions I lost marks on.

marking.html:
1. 400 ÷ 0.8 = 500 (1) N/m² or Pa (1).
  2. Heels have a smaller area (1); the same force/weight on a smaller area (1) gives a bigger pressure (1).
  3. The air particles get more energy and move faster (1); they hit the walls harder / more often (1); so the pressure inside increases and pushes the rubber out (1).
  4. It decreases (1); there is less air above you / the air is less dense (1).
  5. 1 mark each for gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, in the right order between the mouth and the anus.
  6. Villi give a big surface area (1); thin wall, so a short distance (1); blood capillaries carry the food away (1).
  7. Fibre adds bulk (1) so the gut muscles can push food along / prevents constipation (1).
  8. (a) 8 − 5 = 3 cm (1). (b) double the force → double the extension: 6 cm (1).
  9. The open parachute has a big area, so air resistance increases (1); air resistance is bigger than her weight, so she slows down (1); as she slows, air resistance falls until it equals her weight: resultant force zero, so steady speed (1).
  10. Friction: oil / grease / lubrication (1). Drag: streamlined shape (1).
  11. In: rib muscles contract, ribs up and out (1); diaphragm contracts and moves down (1); chest volume increases and pressure decreases, so air is drawn in (1). Out: muscles relax, ribs down and in, diaphragm up (1); volume decreases (1); pressure increases, so air is pushed out (1).

Total: 33 marks. In the explain questions, a mark only counts if the link is there (for example “smaller area so bigger pressure”).
